newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee lower as call rates ease.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee lower as call rates ease.

text.p: Sri Lankan call money rates eased on Thursday, increasing demand for dollars and pushing down the rupee, dealers said.
The rupee was quoted at 56.64 to the dollar at 0500 GMT after opening at 56.60, which was down from its previous closing level of 56.57.
"Call money has eased and there is genuine demand for dollars created mainly by rice imports," said a local bank dealer.
The government has been importing rice regularly to offset shortages caused by severe drought this year.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by 1.5 local cents, and fixed buying and selling at 55.9820 and 57.1130.
Call money rates were down at 15 percent after closing at 22 percent on Wednesday.
Dealers said there were more lenders than borrowers in the market, as some banks had discounted treasury bills in favour of call and term lending.
